title: Choose Virtue
coreMove: Stillness gets sturdier when conduct is clean: treat virtue as enough, write the honest action first, and stop asking approval to bless what conscience already knows.

exampleSpecs.domain: restaurant expediting at the pass window
exampleSpecs.audience: Readers tempted to let approval reorder a fair queue
exampleSpecs.stakes: A reviewer in the dining room could make favoritism feel like greatness.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Denise and Keith let the ticket order, not reviewer approval, decide the next plate.

exampleSpecs.audience: Readers under pressure to protect a clean-looking dashboard
exampleSpecs.stakes: A late update can preserve appearance while adding inner conflict.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Vincent breaks the expected image-control move by posting the delay before complaints force it.

exampleSpecs.audience: Readers facing a tiny shortcut in a public line
exampleSpecs.stakes: A small dishonest scan can start to feel normal when the line is impatient.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Anais and Gisele let repeated character, not line pressure, decide the refund.

exampleSpecs.audience: Readers whose routine gets bent by a familiar face
exampleSpecs.stakes: A rushed exception can make equal rules feel optional.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lionel pauses, restarts the script, and uses the same check-in rule again.

exampleSpecs.audience: Readers tempted to make accuracy serve applause
exampleSpecs.stakes: The viral clip would win approval by making the guest sound worse.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Gisele leaves the accurate answer intact even though the sharper clip would get more attention.

exampleSpecs.audience: Readers who want calm without the cost of clean conduct
exampleSpecs.stakes: A parent complaint can punish the tutor who refused to trade learning for appearance.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The evidence shows Heath kept the student's work honest before the complaint arrived.
